The New York Knicks are an American professional basketball team based in New York City. They compete in the National Basketball Association (NBA) as a member club of the league's Eastern Conference Atlantic Division. Founded in 1946, they are one of the NBA's original teams and have a rich history filled with notable players, coaches, and rivalries.
Key Points:
The Knicks were founded in 1946 as the New York Knickerbockers.
They play their home games at Madison Square Garden in Manhattan.
Notable former players include Patrick Ewing, Willis Reed, and Carmelo Anthony.
Key rivalries include Boston Celtics, Brooklyn Nets, Chicago Bulls, Indiana Pacers, and Miami Heat.
The team has won 10 division titles and reached the NBA Finals twice (1973, 1999).
Current head coach is Tom Thibodeau since 2020.
Notable Events:
1968: Willis Reed leads Knicks to their only NBA championship.
1994: Patrick Ewing and the Knicks win the Eastern Conference title.
2012: Carmelo Anthony helps Knicks return to the playoffs after a 7-year absence.
2015: The team introduces new "New Look" uniforms inspired by their 1990s blue era.
Rivalries:
Boston Celtics: Long-standing rivalry between two of the NBA's original teams.
Brooklyn Nets: Geographical and interdivisional rival with similar fan bases.
Chicago Bulls: Intense rivalry during late 80s/early 90s featuring Michael Jordan vs. Patrick Ewing.
Indiana Pacers: Strong divisional rivalry from 1993 to early 2000s.
Recent Developments:
In the 2024 NBA playoffs, the Knicks were upset by the Indiana Pacers in a seven-game series.
The team signed Jalen Brunson as a free agent in July 2022 and acquired Carmelo Anthony via trade that same month.
Scott Perry was named President of Basketball Operations in March 2017.
The New York Knicks continue to be one of the most storied franchises in NBA history, with passionate fans and a rich tradition.
